title:
Go Again
Seven Times
paragraphs: Notice what the servant never does: he never softens the report to make Elijah feel better, and he never argues with the prophet for sending him back up the mountain again. Six times he climbs, looks at a flat, empty sea, and comes down to say the same true thing — there is nothing. Elijah doesn't rebuke him for the bad news and he doesn't pray louder. He just says go again, as if the previous six nothings were simply the cost of getting to the seventh look.

That's the part of breakthrough nobody frames and hangs on the wall: the climbing that produces nothing you can point to, five and six times in a row, while the sky stays exactly the way it's always been. But the cloud that finally rises is only a hand's width wide — small enough to miss if you'd quit on climb number six. Whatever you're watching for today, the instruction hasn't changed. Go again.
